text: On the chat_preference testbed, a two-phase curriculum — training first on the most-confident half of the data, then continuing on the full dataset at a lower learning rate — yielded a PGR of 0.68. This is the only metric reported for the run, and it should be read with substantial caution. The configuration does not specify num_seeds, so the number of replicates behind this value is unknown and no estimate of run-to-run variability is available; a single reported figure cannot be distinguished from noise without such information. No baseline PGR is provided either, so the 0.68 cannot be characterized as better or worse than a standard one-phase training procedure, nor can any gain be attributed to the curriculum structure or the reduced learning rate in the second phase. Further runs with multiple seeds and a matched baseline would be needed before drawing any comparative conclusion about this method's effect.
